newsitem.title: THAILAND: Sitca says may take stake in Thai bank.
newsitem.headline: Sitca says may take stake in Thai bank.

text.p: Sitca Investment and Securities Plc said on Tuesday it was considering a 750 million baht ($29 million) investment to take a five percent stake in medium-sized Bangkok Metropolitan Bank Plc.
Following a decision to increase registered capital by more than five billion baht, the bank recently appointed Sitca as its financial advisor.
Sitca would continue trying to privately place the bank's new shares but would consider taking a stake in the bank if the capital increase was undersubscribed, the statement said.

"The company ... might also consider taking BMB's shares, worth not more than 750 million baht or five percent of the bank's registered capital, in case shares remain after allocation to other investors," it added.
"However no agreement or conclusion on subscribing to these new shares have been reached so far," it added, though senior executives at Sitca said talks with the bank were ongoing.
Following the statement the exchange lifted a halt placed on trading of Sitca's stock this morning.
Thai newspapers had earlier reported that Sitca was poised to take a stake in the bank.
At 0752 GMT Sitca's shares had lost 0.25 baht to 17.25. Bangkok Metrolpolitan Bank Plc shares had gained 0.10 baht at 8.50. The composite market SET Index was up 0.40 percent to 717.33.
Sitca Investment and Securities Plc, a middle ranking finance and securities firm, has repeatedly tried to move into the commercial banking sector.
A Sitca led consortium's failed in its bid to win a new commercial banking licence last year.
The firm also recently gave up a bid to take over the running of failed Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc after negotiations with the central bank on conditions broke down.
